reason: A fresh full-corpus formal run at reasoning effort max on the candidate built from the latest main of the source repository (0.0.3-beta.38 / 3ecccb40), repeating the max condition that was last measured on beta.37 (run 36296596889). That earlier max run was not scoreable: 5 of its 30 cells carried no verdict (3 datacurve cells died pre-model on a public.ecr.aws 429 image-pull throttle, 2 terminal-bench cells errored when a single model call hit the CLI's own 840s per-call ceiling). candidateDeltaAudit.reading: Unlike beta.34 -> beta.36 and beta.36 -> beta.37, this transition is NOT entirely inert: there is one model-visible change (thread tool v2 schema). The timeout, prompt and context paths that produced every measured failure and latency figure are unchanged, so the max-effort latency behaviour (including the two cells that hit the client's 840s per-call ceiling) is expected to persist. Any verdict difference must therefore be read as that small tool-schema delta plus run-to-run variance, and never as a broad capability claim.

corpusPin.batchPlan: config/frontier-harness-batches.json exact-covers the frozen corpus in corpus order (3 tracked batches, 30 unique tasks)

provider.note: max is the frozen profile's own declared default and is materialized into every per-task record; the report refuses an undeclared effort.

knownRisks.ecrThrottle: The beta.37 max run lost 3 datacurve cells pre-model to a public.ecr.aws pull throttle (`429 toomanyrequests: Data limit exceeded`) while building 8 images concurrently. The condition is kept at fh_max_parallel=8 for fidelity with the source formal run, so the throttle may recur. If it does, those cells are pre-model environment failures and are recoverable through the repository's recovery channel (exactly as batch recovery-no-prediction-20260927 recovered the beta.37 ones).
knownRisks.perCallCeiling: polyglot-c-py and regex-log errored twice at reasoning effort max because their first model call outran the CLI's own --model-timeout-ms 840000 ceiling (measured 840.021s/840.022s and 840.021s/840.026s in two independent dispatches). The timeout pipeline is byte-identical in beta.38, so the same outcome is expected. If it recurs, the cells stay verdict-less, the run stays not scoreable, and per the repository's rules nothing is retried: only an explicitly authorized change to the per-call ceiling or to the effort condition could give those cells a verdict, and neither is made here.

constraints: One predeclared headless attempt per task, all 30 Docker-eligible corpus tasks, one frozen candidate, the official agent and verifier budgets preserved (fh_agent_timeout_multiplier=1) and never extended.

This run's pass@1 comes only from its own frozen aggregate report. It is never merged with run 36092882496, with the beta.37 max run, or with any diagnostic batch, and it replaces or reinterprets none of their verdicts.
No condition is changed to make the run scoreable: the per-call ceiling, the budgets and the effort stay exactly as the frozen composition declares them.
Nothing is published to main and no other run is cancelled, restarted or re-dispatched.
